name: Shell
description: The talk-to-everything terminal: prefix commands create records, bare text goes to AI chat with the user's model and MCP tool subset. Talk is the same conversation projected as a voice-first stage. This version makes the AI turn record SERVER-AUTHORITATIVE: /api/ai/chat writes every turn to shell_commands itself -- stamped created_at, session_id (minted by the page per load), source surface, model, duration_ms, and the tool calls actually made -- before the reply is even sent, so history survives whatever the page does next. The client-side fire-and-forget write it replaces lost a real turn when the page died first, carried no timestamp, and grouped nothing; an evening of live debugging against those rows is what forced the change. Non-AI command turns (note/link/search) stay client-written: they never touch the chat endpoint, and the server cannot record what it never sees. This is the substrate for q9-style session listing and resume -- sessions become a fold over turns, not a second table.
